contexts.text: So that the man is a mere congeries and composition of evils and falsities.
There are as many spheres as there are affections, and compositions of affections.
The idea of many things, which may be collected into one compound idea...
They cease in unities... When in composites they glide on by an accent...
There is nothing which, however simple it may appear, is not composite, and which does not come forth from what is prior to itself.
Exteriors cannot enter into interiors, as composites into simples, thus not the things of the body into those of the spirit; but contrariwise. SE 2301:end.
For lower things are nothing but compounds of higher ones, as may be inferred from the memories...

They who are in inmost perception are in perception of all things which are beneath, for the things which are beneath are nothing but derivations and compounds therefrom; for what is inmost is all in all of the lower things...
Hence it is that the forms and material substances with man are of the same character, but in a lower degree, because they are grosser and more composite.
Interior things are component, and those which are exterior are composite.

The derivations in the lower degrees are only compositions, or rather conformations of the singulars and particulars of the higher degrees in succession, with such things added from purer nature, and then from grosser, as may serve for containing vessels...
In themselves, exterior things are grosser than interior ones, for they are generals compounded of a host of interior things.
So that the understanding is nothing but a compound of such things as relate to truths, and the will is nothing but an affection of such things as are called goods.
In each and all things in the whole world... there are such degrees of production and of composition, namely, that from one thing there is a second, and from the second a third, and so on.
The interiors of the Angels are compounded to the heavenly form.
Each general use is compounded of innumerable things which may be called mediate, administerial, and subservient uses.
Hypocrites... have contracted a habit of composing their interiors to an imitation of good affections.
All a man's loves relate to his reigning love, and make one with it, or together compose it. HH 486:end.
He composes his face to devotion.
These degrees... are as simples, as congregates of these, and again as congregates of these, which taken together are called a composite.

All things in the world which are of trinal dimension, or which are called composites, consist of discrete degrees. For example... every muscle consists of least fibres, and these compounded fascicularly present the larger fibres which are called motor fibres, and from bundles of these there exists the composite which is called a muscle.
The second discrete degree is from the first, and the third from the second; the third being called the composite.
Woody filaments from the leasts to their composite are homogeneous.
In the extremes... are the parts compounded of these...
The outermost is compounded of these...

The inmosts, middles, and outermosts of the parts are in these degrees, for they are successive compositions, or confasciations and conglobations, from simples, which are their first substances or matters.
It is asserted by some that there is a substance so simple that it is not a form from lesser forms, and that from this substance substantiate or composite things arise by coacervation...
The Hells in the composite are called the devil and satan.
Thoughts are nothing but affections compounded into forms by the life's love, so as to appear in light.
Through His Divine Providence, the Lord composes affections into one form, which is the human. General article.
From the elegance and neatness of the composition of the words...
Affections... form the will, and make and compose it.
Suppose a society composed of mere devils, and a society composed of mere Angels...
That order may exist in a compound society...
Alternate quarrellings and adjustments of differences...
By influx is meant all that which precedes, and composes what follows. Example(s).
In minds, all things which precede form series, and the series gather themselves together, one next another, and one after another, and these together compose the ultimate.
You are in beginnings and thus in singulars, but we are in derivatives and composites; you are in particulars, but we are in generals...
In man there are all affections of love, and thence all perceptions of wisdom compounded in the most perfect order... Since the human form is compounded of these...

Discrete degrees are generations and compositions of the one from the other; as for example, of a nerve from its fibres, and of a fibre from its fibrils; or of a piece of wood, stone, or metal from its parts, and of a part from its particles.
Man in the composite... is the neighbour. General article.
Those who enter into a society compose as it were one body.
The man of the Church in the compound, or composite... is the Church among many...
Nothing can exist in the composite or in the general, unless it be from its simples or parts...
The lower things of life are more obscure in proportion as they are more composite; from their very composition and form they derive the fact that the life is such as it appears.
This whole composite idea... SE 4037.
(A kind of composite animal described.)
Every composition in nature has been effected through these degrees; for if you unroll anything composite you will see that therein one thing is from another, to the outermost...
